subject: Political Science
central_question: What does it mean to treat people as equals, and which political, social and economic measures can reduce unjust and entrenched inequality?
in_scope_units: Why Does Equality Matter: equal human worth, historical struggles and visible global and Indian inequalities.
What is Equality: equal respect, equality of opportunity and the distinction between natural and socially produced inequality.
Three Dimensions of Equality: political, social and economic equality.
Feminism, Marxism, liberalism and socialism as competing explanations and remedies for inequality.
How Can We Promote Equality: formal equality, differential treatment and affirmative action.
banned_topics: The harm principle and negative versus positive liberty, which belong to Freedom.
Detailed principles of distributive justice and Rawls’ veil of ignorance, which belong to Social Justice.
Detailed constitutional provisions and remedies, which belong to the Indian Constitution at Work textbook.

known_pitfalls.claim: Equality requires identical treatment in every circumstance.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter allows differential treatment when it is necessary to secure equal rights and opportunities.

known_pitfalls.claim: All inequalities are natural and therefore unchangeable.
known_pitfalls.correction: Many inequalities result from social power, discrimination and unequal opportunities and can be altered.

known_pitfalls.claim: Political equality automatically creates social and economic equality.
known_pitfalls.correction: Equal legal rights may coexist with unequal access to education, health, income and social respect.

known_pitfalls.claim: Feminism treats every difference between women and men as biological.
known_pitfalls.correction: Feminism distinguishes biological sex from socially assigned gender roles and challenges patriarchy.

known_pitfalls.claim: Affirmative action is always a permanent privilege.
known_pitfalls.correction: It is presented as special, justified assistance intended to overcome entrenched disadvantage and enable fair competition.

recommended_example_progression: Begin with NCERT Exercise Q1 on natural and socially created inequality.
Use NCERT Exercise Q5 to distinguish discrimination from justified differential treatment.
Use NCERT Exercise Q2 to examine economic equality without absolute sameness.
Use NCERT Exercise Q6 to test arguments for women’s political equality.
Conclude with NCERT Exercise Q4 on targeted assistance to disadvantaged farmers.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The end-of-chapter Exercises contain Questions 1–6 on natural and social inequality, economic gaps, equal rights, opportunity, affirmative action and differential treatment.
